title: restrictedGrafanaApis: how to add a new restricted API and wire a new mutation command/document type
answers: How do I expose a new privileged API to app plugins?
Where is the allow/block-list / feature-toggle gating for plugin access to restricted APIs?
What do I need to touch to add a new dashboard/notebook mutation command?
What do I need to touch to support a new mutable document type (not dashboard/notebook)?
body:
Adding a restricted API is a 3-file change (per `public/app/features/plugins/components/restrictedGrafanaApis/README.md`): (1) add the API file under `restrictedGrafanaApis/`, (2) register it in the `restrictedGrafanaApis` object in `RestrictedGrafanaApisProvider.tsx` (gated by `config.featureToggles.restrictedPluginApis`), (3) add the field to `RestrictedGrafanaApisContextType` in `packages/grafana-data/src/context/plugins/RestrictedGrafanaApis.tsx` — it must stay optional there or the type guard breaks the build. The provider is mounted with a `pluginId` at `AppRootPage.tsx` (app plugin pages) and `plugins/extensions/utils.tsx` (extension points); allow/block-list enforcement by pluginId happens inside `RestrictedGrafanaApisContextProvider` in that same `@grafana/data` file, not in this folder.

For the `dashboardMutationAPI` specifically: a new mutation command must be added to `DASHBOARD_COMMANDS`/`NOTEBOOK_COMMANDS` so `commandRegistry.ts:allMutationCommands()` (the union of both, used by `dashboardMutationApi.ts:getPayloadSchema/getAvailableCommands`) can discover it even when that document type isn't mounted — adding the command's execute-time handling alone is not enough. A new mountable document type needs: a new `MutationResource` value in `dashboard-scene/mutation-api/clientBridge.ts`, a branch in the callback passed to `provideMutationClientFactory` (registered in `dashboardMutationApi.ts`), and the scene calling `createMutationClient` on activation / tearing it down on deactivation.
